I completed GTA 6's indie game darling pastiche, Tenebrae Lux, and all I got was this lousy sense of accomplishment

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1296 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "We are but Promethean wanderers on the fringes of oblivion, clinging to a semblance of light amidst the vast abyss of our own ignorance.
  • Industry observers note that developed, seemingly single-handedly, by an eccentric developer called Johannes Zuch - auteur, pseud, charlatan - you first get introduced to this curious little experiment in one of GTA 6's earliest missions, where protagonist Jason is forced to play it during a 'lad's night in' with buddy Cal.
  • Sources indicate that the first thing I notice about Tenebrae Lux is the name.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"We are but Promethean wanderers on the fringes of oblivion, clinging to a semblance of light amidst the vast abyss of our own ignorance. Voyaging uncharted waters may appear foolish to some, yet folly and heroism can often appear the same to the undiscerning eye," so indicates the voice of Johannes Zuch - creator, writer, director, composer, and 'perceptual architect' behind Leonida's latest favourite indie darling art game, Tenebrae Lux. It's pretentious, it's deeply up its own arse, and it's awkward and off-putting to play. A must-review for Eurogamer.

Industry observers note that developed, seemingly single-handedly, by an eccentric developer called Johannes Zuch - auteur, pseud, charlatan - you first get introduced to this curious little experiment in one of GTA 6's earliest missions, where protagonist Jason is forced to play it during a 'lad's night in' with buddy Cal. Jason is quick to dismiss Tenebrae Lux in manufacturer, but once Cal slinks off home - hungover and dreary - I slide the disc back into my JoyStation console and sink my teeth back into it. Jason loves this stuff, really. He only keeps Time Jackers: Rewind installed so his mates don't judge him.

Sources indicate that the first thing I notice about Tenebrae Lux is the name. It's Latin for 'darkness and light', or something similar. Is this riffing on Clair Obscur, which is French for 'light dark'? No, it's too cerebral for that - too plodding and navel-gazey. Sandfall Interactive wouldn't be this pretentious. Maybe it's a pastiche of Dear Esther, then, drawing on the tenets and schema of the 'walking simulator' genre and using that washed-out film noir aesthetic. But then, it's too wordy for that, with too many interactive and puzzle-adjacent elements. Ah, it must be mocking The Witness, instead - there's the telltale lighthouse, the 'I'm definitely not telling you where to go and what to do' internal narration, and of course the fingerprints of Johannes Zuch are all over it. Johannes Zuch, Jonathan Blow - see how they braided them together? (Sorry).

Whilst this has been created by Rockstar as a pastiche - as much loving send-up as it is withering take down - and designed to make a quick joke in the early 'Feng Shui' mission, the game is playable from start to finish if you so desire. You boot it up by inserting a physical disc, too, which is funny given the context. And it's good! Well, not good good, but it's a proper brainteaser, and ribs 2016's The Witness with such knowledge and (I think?) respect that it's hard not to be charmed by Rockstar's game-within-a-game. There are collectibles to be found that riff on Mark Z. Danielewski's House of Leaves, too, a knowing nod to the most try-hard of all try-hard literature.

Within seconds of the title screen, too, you're presented with a game-within-a-game-within-a-game. You must clear four boards filled with puzzle pieces as the protagonist mutters something mysterious and weird in his posh voice. Do so, and you unlock the door to the next location. Head up to a bunker, and you'll see a room filled with various clues - maybe it's a flashing lamp flickering in morse code, maybe it's a malfunctioning clock presenting a maths puzzle, maybe it's a pricetag on a record that changes on every visit, maybe it's a photograph with anomalous elements, maybe it's a "Developed Using Zuchworks Engine" easter egg hidden in the environment. You need to keep your wits about you, because one of these clues changes every time you enter - and the clue corresponds to a date that changes on a calendar on the wall.

It has been revealed that you can look up a guide if you need to, or you can spend far too long figuring out how all this relates to the telephone you can find in the room on your own, like muggins here, before opening up the path to the next puzzle. Look at the image below to see the level of record-keeping and brainteasing this bizarre little game prompted from me. I will say, the sense of achievement you get from playing around with this stuff is pretty remarkable, given - let's not forget I'm actually playing Grand Theft Auto 6 whilst I'm wandering around in the black and white murk trying to complete a puzzle game for no actual reward.

The bunker room is, by far, the hardest part of Tenebrae Lux. From here, things ease up: you need to figure out the right sequence of glyphs on a bridge, and then put some distance between yourself and a curious and rather creepy suited man that's seemingly figuring things out ahead of you in a location inspired by, I think, The Backrooms (or Portal, or Superliminal, or maybe something else entirely. Who knows what Zuch was thinking?).

"With the last enigma finally mastered," the narrator drones in his bumbling monotone, "I step forward into the void, the shadows swallow, consuming all, and then finally the sweet embrace of darkness of which there is no end." 'You have just experienced a Johannes Zuch experience', Tenebrae Lux tells me, before cutting to the best joke of the whole thing: the credits roll much akin to something Hideo Kojima would produce.

In a recent development, so, what do you get out of all of this? Well - just like real puzzle games in the real world - nothing, really. If you've not completed one of the other three fully playable games in GTA 6, you will get a trophy/achievement. But given the main game is all about Jason and Lucia's desperate scramble to escape the poverty trap, to try and break free of the cycle of debt, violence, and consequence that keeps them clinging to Leonida's seedy underbelly, there's no monetary reward. There's no 'progress' in the sense of the protagonist's shared story.

Industry observers note that even in terms of your own cold, hard, mathematical 'completion' you only need to boot each of the four games up once in order to work towards GTA 6's 100% completion. So what's the point of all this? Why did I spend the better part of 90 minutes trying to figure out how to find a sliver of light in the dark in Tenebrae Lux? The game is a wonderful pastiche in that, essentially, it's not really saying anything. You can probably project some vague meaning onto it if you wish - I'm pretty certain the protagonist literally 'finds himself' at the end - but glib little readings like that are ten-a-penny in this genre.

Sources indicate that I think the most impressive thing about Tenebrae Lux is that it exists. You're teased with it in an early mission - Rockstar may as well say 'look, we put a game in a game, lol' - but it's more than that. This is what happens when Rockstar's 4700-plus developers are given the room to… develop. Tenebrae Lux could very easily have been a non-interactive experience, a quick, cheap joke shown over-the-shoulder taking a drive-by pop shot at Johnathan Blow, Hideo Kojima, Dan Pinchbeck, or any and all of the above. Or maybe it could be a 'vertical slice', an incomplete demo, a teaser. But it's not, because nothing about GTA 6 is quick or cheap.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6, in every single conceivable way, is a premium experience - part-sandbox, part-simulation, part-otherworld. To create not just one, but four fully playable and completable games within that framework is showboating, sure, but to make that game actually good and - perhaps controversially - even better than some of the games it's pastiching… Well, it's just rubbing salt in the wound, really.

A code for the game was provided by Cal Hampton.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been a wild ride for Google Pixel’s App Lock feature, but the company is officially re-releasing the feature today, right alongside its debut on Samsung Galaxy devices.

Industry observers note that app Lock debuted on Google Pixel in an August build of Android 17 QPR2’s beta. The feature lets people hide apps behind a biometric or PIN authentication layer while also hiding notifications, widgets, and data from AI services. It’s a useful privacy features, but one that Google removed in subsequent updates. The feature later returned in QPR3 Beta 3 last month, and today Google is officially re-releasing it.

The feature is still only in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 3 for Google Pixel devices, an update that should be released to the stable track in early 2027.

Industry observers note that pixel owners on stable Android 17 QPR2 should already have this! Why would Google make Pixel owners wait until March 2027 to get this?! Release it now to Pixel owners. 🤨.

You can still access App Lock by long-pressing on an app icon and adding it to the app lock list.

In a post on Reddit, Google’s Community Engagement Manager details that App Lock on Google Pixel was removed for improvements before getting a full release:.

…the product team decided to temporarily pull back the feature from the QPR2 Beta to allow for additional polish, thorough testing, and robust integration across all system surfaces.

Industry observers note that that’s why Samsung’s One UI 9.5 beta release today also brings support for App Lock. The feature is built into Android 17 QPR2, seemingly the release that One UI 9.5 is based on, but Google Pixel devices aren’t getting it until QPR3. As far as release timelines go, this means that Samsung’s Galaxy S27 series will probably ship with this feature out of the box, where Pixel phones won’t get it until around March or so. One UI 9.5 won’t roll out for older Galaxy devices until May, if One UI 8.5 serves as an example.

Tech Report: GTA VI runs at 1440p on PS5 and Xbox Series X, but just 720p with upscaling on Series S

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (500 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the most highly anticipated video game of the decade is here.
  • It has been revealed that in a statement shared with Wccftech, the technical team at Rockstar has confirmed that GTA VI uses different upscaling solutions across all consoles in order to achieve a balance between visual quality and performance with a target of 30FPS.
  • It has been revealed that as for rendered resolutions, the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, and PlayStation 5 Pro all start with a native base resolution of 1440p, which is then upscaled to 4K.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the most highly anticipated video game of the decade is here. GTA VI arrives almost 13 years after GTA V, with reports suggesting that it has already generated around $1.54 billion in revenue from 16 million preorders. Ahead of its release, Rockstar Games has finally shared some technical details, including rendering resolutions and upscaling technologies being used across all consoles.

It has been revealed that in a statement shared with Wccftech, the technical team at Rockstar has confirmed that GTA VI uses different upscaling solutions across all consoles in order to achieve a balance between visual quality and performance with a target of 30FPS. The PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X use Rockstar's own temporal anti-aliasing (TAA) solution, while the PlayStation 5 Pro relies on Sony's second-generation PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR2). The Xbox Series S, meanwhile, relies on AMD's FSR 4 upscaling technology.

It has been revealed that as for rendered resolutions, the PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, and PlayStation 5 Pro all start with a native base resolution of 1440p, which is then upscaled to 4K. The Xbox Series S is the least powerful console; thus, the game runs at a lower base resolution of 720p, which is upscaled to 1080p using FSR 4. The final image on all consoles is then composited with a 4K user interface before being presented.

Industry observers note that rockstar has also developed a physically-based material library for GTA VI and a cinematic imaging pipeline to deliver realistic lighting, reflections, and material details within the game. The team states it has worked to maintain a consistent lighting solution across all consoles, including the Xbox Series S, while adjusting ray-traced global illumination (RTGI) features depending on each platform's hardware capabilities.

Sources indicate that the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S launched all the way back in 2020, and while the consoles have capable hardware, their architectures are finally beginning to show their age. The fact that Rockstar is targeting just 30FPS across all consoles, while relying on different upscaling technologies and rendering resolutions, highlights how much performance is potentially being left on the table in order to maintain visual fidelity. That being stated, a PC release of GTA VI continues to be a big question mark. Rockstar is yet to announce a release date or even provide a launch window, meaning that PC gamers can only rely on Xbox Cloud Gaming to stream the game on their systems.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fortnite’s PlayStation Cup is back in November, giving PlayStation players a chance to compete for a share of $100,000 in cash prizes.

The cup qualifiers start on November 23, with separate competitions for Battle Royale and Zero Build. Both are Solo events, so you can jump in without having to find a duo partner or put a squad together.

Here’s how to enter the Fortnite PlayStation Cup on your PlayStation, when each round takes place, and what you can win.

Industry observers note that before the Cup starts, make sure your PlayStation and Epic Games accounts are linked and that you’ve enabled two-factor authentication. Your Epic account needs to be in good standing and at least level 50, which you can check in the Career tab. You’ll also need to be at least 13 and meet the eligibility requirements for your country.

The Cup starts on Monday, November 23, with qualifiers for both Battle Royale and Zero Build. Top 80 players who advance in Zero Build will compete in the finals on Tuesday, November 24, while the Battle Royale finals take place on Wednesday, November 25.

This gives you just one day to book a spot in the finals, so you’ll have to rack up those wins as swiftly as possible.

Industry observers note that each mode has $50,000 in prize money split across seven regions. In Europe, the top 50 finishers in each final earn cash, with $4,000 going to first place. North America Central also pays out to the top 50, with $2,500 for the winner.

In North America West, Brazil, the Middle East, Oceania, and Asia, the top 25 players in each final earn a cash prize, with $750 for first place.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Motorola has kicked off its Android 17 rollout for the Razr Fold, marking the first major patch for the organization’s first book-style foldable, and the start of a potentially interest 7 years of software support.

Industry observers note that the Motorola Razr Fold launched with Android 16 back in May 2026, and it remains a really good option for those looking to pick up a book-style foldable in the US. On top of solid specs across the board, it also carries the promise of 7 years of software support, something that few other Moto devices can tout.

But nowhere was it promises that Motorola would speed things up at all. A little over 3 months after Motorola revealed the update and several weeks after other Motorola devices were updated to Android 17, the Motorola Razr Fold is finally getting its own Android 17 update.

Rolling out now, Android 17 for the Razr Fold is a 4.15GB~ update that appears to be available at least somewhat broadly. Reports are popping up on Reddit including one report from the EU (Hungary, specifically), with another user apparently in a Spanish-speaking region also seeing the update.

We’re still waiting to see if the upgrade is available in the US (there’s a backlog of updates on our unit), but it’s certainly an update to look forward to. Apparently, Motorola finally fixed a weird UI matter that affected the Telegram app, something we ran into when using the device earlier this year.

In a recent development, it’s great to see the update out, but it’s noteworthy that Motorola is not setting a particularly encouraging precedent here. Razr Fold is one of the company’s first devices to be promised 7 years of OS updates and software support, and its flagship-tier status certainly would have most expecting it to be updated ahead of some of Motorola’s more affordable, lower-tier devices that were updated over a month ago. Whatever the case, hopefully Motorola will speed things up over the next few years, especially with its $1,600 flagship Signature 27 on the horizon with the same software promises.

Nvidia today held its first all-hands meeting since the resignation of co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang. According to Wired, interim CEO Colette Kress offered more money and equity on a faster-than-expected schedule to calm staffers' nerves."So I’m here to tell you, the best thing that we want to do is to take care of each and every single employee that is here and to make sure that you feel good about this company and you do not worry about your comp,” Wired reports Kress said.The pay and equity bumps are set for December, far ahead of the company's normal raise cycle. One director-level employee has already written to the board and top executives, warning that failure to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive could lead to the loss of ‘irreplaceable talent.’.

According to recent reports, A potential exodus of talent could also spook investors, despite standout earnings on Thursday. It took me less than an hour to find my first incredibly minor Rockstar easter egg in GTA 6 - but it has some major implications for Leonida

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that are you wondering how connected the worlds of GTA 5 and GTA 6 are?
  • In a recent development, right, if you're reading from this point onwards, you're clearly here for the tea.
  • Sources indicate that called 'Body Copy' - a joke I appreciate as a former magazine editor, naturally - this publication features a few different articles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that are you wondering how connected the worlds of GTA 5 and GTA 6 are? Well, I've got some news for you. Keep on reading below if you'd like some very minor spoilers for the early game of GTA 6, spoilers for GTA 5, as well as some information about how the new game links to GTA 5 and other Rockstar games.

In a recent development, right, if you're reading from this point onwards, you're clearly here for the tea. In the first hour or so of GTA 6, when you finally get control of Jason and head to your first property (the green stilted house) in the Leonida Keys, you will be able to explore a little. On my way to do a workout - you need to keep Jason a peak physical instrument for his work's sake, right? Right? - I happened upon a fitness magazine resting on a table on the decking out front.

Sources indicate that called 'Body Copy' - a joke I appreciate as a former magazine editor, naturally - this publication features a few different articles. There's Morning Glory, where Nolan Crockett jacks you with his early workout; Skindecent Exposure, a photo spread about why beaches are 'crazy' places to work out; Shrediquette, a piece dedicated to proper in-gym decorum; and Twilight Tantra, an interview feature and yoga masterclass with 'gerontophile' Fabien LaRouche.

Hang on, Fabien LaRouche… isn't that the French wellness guru and shyster that was a "close friend" to Amanda De Santa in Grand Theft Auto 5? Yes, yes it is. In fact, Fabien played quite a large role in that game, acting as the antagonistic force that eventually fractured Michael and Amanda's relationship. After conducting an affair under the guise of 'yoga lessons', Amanda left our protagonist, and moved in with Fabien, taking Michael's kids - Jimmy and Tracy - with her. In a totally healthy and normal way, you could follow their new life via updates posted to GTA's Facebook surrogate, LifeInvader. It's clear the kids never liked the pretentious, annoying man - but for Amanda, the penny is a little slower to drop. Eventually, Amanda and Michael reconcile their differences - with the latter whalloping Fabien in the process. The married couple pledge to resolve their differences, and Fabien is never seen again.

Sources indicate that until GTA 6, at least. Here, in what we assume is supposed to be 2025 or 2026, it's been about 13 years since we last saw the character (it is widely agreed that GTA 5 is set in 2013 - the game's original launch year). And it seems that the events surrounding Michael and his family really did a number on Fabien. Which - of course - he blamed on the universe, rather than taking any personal responsibility. Naturally.

"Ever since the karmic decay of Los Santos was made perfectly clear to him in the early 2010s, yoga instructor Fabien LaRouche has been on an epic pilgrimage of enlightenment through the remotest ashrams and finest 5-star resorts and plastic surgery retreats of The East," reads the Body Copy article. "Having completed his chakric education and returned to the United States, we meet with him on the final week of his six-month residency at Dwindle Wood Retirement Community.".

Here, the article goes on to explore Fabien's penchant for older women - he seems to like their nature, their desire to learn about self-improvement and wellness, and (perhaps most importantly) their bank accounts. "Being over the hill doesn't necessarily mean you have nothing left to live for," he opines in the article. Thanks for that, Fabien.

Industry observers note that it's interesting to see - very early in the game and quite plainly telegraphed - that Rockstar is willing to reintroduce us to people from previous games. This isn't a megaton addition by any means - Fabien was never a 'main character' - but I love that a nod to him, in a feature tucked away at the back of a magazine, sets the scene for more cameos, perhaps, later in the game. It highlights us, nice and early, that GTA 5 and GTA 6 are indeed connected. By inference, then, we know that GTA 4 is included in that same picture; there were recurring characters in GTA 5 that appeared in GTA 4, after all - Patrick McReary, Johnny Klebitz, Rocco Pelosi and more come to mind.

It may seem like a small thing, but it's just another example of Rockstar using its expansive toolset, ridiculous budget, and well-established legacy to inject a sense of scale into the world of Grand Theft Auto 6. There are other nods to the universe out there, too. I won't spoil them here, but I've been a little bit dewy-eyed to hear rumours of some of the other nods to Rockstar titles hidden in the world of Leonida: it makes all the experiences I've had in past games, the emotional response I've had to previous Rockstar worlds, feel in some way valid and meaningful here, too. I'm looking forward to seeing what other little secrets await me across the keys and into the glowing neon promise of Vice City proper.

#70050. Nvidia GeForce driver bug reportedly hammers SSDs with up to 30GB of writes per hour

📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (742 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Tomshardware ↗ Open Full Page

Nvidia GeForce driver bug reportedly hammers SSDs with up to 30GB of writes per hour

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (742 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia’s GeForce driver 621.14 is reportedly causing excessive background writes on idle PCs, inducing extra wear on SSDs.
  • The bug is described by user Andergraude in an Nvidia forum post as “fresh in 621.14,” which came out on Nov.
  • Sources indicate that the “real writes” point comes from the fact that a per-process write counter is not the same as writes reaching the drive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia’s GeForce driver 621.14 is reportedly causing excessive background writes on idle PCs, inducing extra wear on SSDs. One user measured about 3GB an hour on the susceptible driver, and another mentioned estimated up to 30GB/hour on the newer 621.24. This follows a similar-looking bug from AMD’s video driver discovered last month.

The bug is described by user Andergraude in an Nvidia forum post as “fresh in 621.14,” which came out on Nov. 4, who indicates it operates by “continuously [rewriting] the binary log file” with “real writes” to the drive. The writes are coming from the NVDisplay.Container.exe process, or the “NVIDIA Display Container LS” service, which logs to the nvlog.nvlgstg file. This background service is necessary for running the Nvidia Control Panel and App. It’s not clear what’s written in the log, and not every system is necessarily impacted.

Sources indicate that the “real writes” point comes from the fact that a per-process write counter is not the same as writes reaching the drive. The measurements came from Windows Resource Monitor, Windows performance counters, and CrystalDiskInfo. The Data Units Written counter matched Windows’ reporting. This test showed 515MB of process I/O coming with 270MB of total writes to the C: drive over five minutes. That works out to roughly 3GB per hour, in line with the user’s own estimate.

Worse, “the write volume increases as the file grows.” Stopping the service and deleting the log can temporarily reduce the writes. With the previous driver version 621.01, the writes totaled less than 2MB per five minutes, and a second user in the thread confirmed that a rollback helps.

In a recent development, mitigation attempts, such as three clean reinstalls with the help of DDU from that second user, did not fix the problem. The writing process also impacted gaming and video performance, potentially causing hitching, which suggests it gets worse under load.

Industry observers note that another user, AyzekUorren, in a separate thread about driver 621.24, which came out Nov. 12, says that it could get up to “about 30gb per 1h” or even “70gb or even more” with longer sessions. This is even with telemetry disabled in the Nvidia App. Noted is that every Alt+Tab added 500MB to 1GB of writes, at least for this user.

In a recent development, in AMD’s case, it was the External Events Utility, or atieclxx.exe, that exhibited constant writes on an idle PC. In that case, the AMD utility was reportedly copying its own executable every second. To put the impact into context, the AMD bug had rates reported between 0.3 and 5MB/s while total drive writes in the 621.14 test measured around 0.9MB/s.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

The Nvidia numbers are somewhat alarming, given that a typical 1TB SSD is rated for 600TB of writes over a standard five-year warranty. Even at 270MB per five minutes, this could be about 28TB per year — for a never-sleeping PC — which is reaching toward 5% of the drive’s rated endurance, although the writes include everything the system is writing and realistic uptime will be less. However, at the higher end — 30GB per hour, at eight hours a day — one could see 15% of drive endurance worn every year for nothing.

According to recent reports, this doesn’t make it a drive killer, but given how much people value drive endurance, especially with SSD prices as they are, avoiding unnecessary writes like this is certainly a priority. To see if you’re affected, check Resource Monitor and look for the telltale NVDisplay.Container.exe and the nvlog.nvlgstg file in the list. You can also check the SMART Data Units Written value with CrystalDiskInfo or equivalent, such as your drive’s SSD toolbox.

At this time, no fix or hotfix has been confirmed, and the best workaround is to do a rollback. A similar matter in the past, fixed with driver update 471.96 back in 2021, was covered by Nvidia’s release notes. As it stands, Nvidia has “N/A” for 621.24’s Open Concerns, and the company has not acknowledged the bug. For the AMD bug, the driver wasn't fixed for over three weeks (and came as an optional update).

Google this week completed the rollout of its fresh gradient icons with updates for Messages and Contacts.

The icon shapes remain the same for all three communication apps, though they are slightly larger and better fill the circular backgrounds. Contacts is still a head and body, while Messages remains overlapping chat bubbles and Phone a handset. This redesign is not particularly disruptive.

Google Contacts was the last Android icon to be refreshed, with version 4.92.26.x rolling out on Wednesday evening. The Phone by Google update rolled out on Monday to stable customers.

It took two weeks from announcement to full availability across the three apps.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, as everyday technology becomes more advanced, parents are prioritizing screen-free, hands-on holiday gifts for children.
  • As everyday technology becomes more advanced, parents are prioritizing screen-free, hands-on holiday gifts for children.
  • Forty-one percent of people buying gifts for kids in their family are leaning toward screen-free gifts, according to a survey by PwC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, as everyday technology becomes more advanced, parents are prioritizing screen-free, hands-on holiday gifts for children. Forty-one percent of people buying gifts for kids in their family are leaning toward screen-free gifts, according to a survey by PwC. A Germany-based brand called Tonies created an interactive, screen-free audio player designed for children. The most well-known toy, called the Toniebox, is a squishy, cube-shaped speaker controlled completely by the child. Models work with hand-painted, magnetic figurines that automatically play audiobooks, songs, or stories when placed on the box. Last holiday season, the Tonies app hit No. 1 on the App Store. This year, the organization saw a 33% increase in global revenue in the first nine months of 2026. Its biggest market is North America, capturing $315 million in revenue in 2025. Concerns about screen use in childhood Screen use in early years of childhood has shown potential to harm cognitive, linguistic, and social-emotional growth, according to a study from the National Library of Medicine. Excessive screen use among youth has even been linked to a rise in likelihood of obesity, sleep disorders, and depression, and anxiety, the study found. Screens have the potential to improve education and learning, when paired with parental controls and screen-time restrictions. But, Tonies offers a chance for children to interact with their minds rather than a touch-screen. “Through listening, the key thing is, your imagination develops because you actually picture the dragon, you picture the knight, you picture whatever it is. It’s not just delivered for you,” Mark McColgan, general manager, North America at Tonies, told Fast Company. The company started producing the Toniebox 10 years ago, and while fresh versions are released, the boxes are built for long-term use, noted McColgan, who joined Tonies this year from Mattel. The boxes are a relief for busy parents, too. Sometimes parents need a moment to themselves, but offering a screen to their children for a short-term distraction can become a long-term addiction, and a source of guilt for parents. Some parents have turned to screens to curb behavior in public, and sometimes, as a replacement for expensive childcare, a study from a hospital found. “It gives them guilt-free time to do something else, because when their child is playing with the Toniebox, they know it’s a safe, good environment for them to do so,” McColgan said. This story was updated to clarify that new versions of the Toniebox have been released since the product launched.

In a recent development, my biggest question isn’t whether gamers will play GTA VI but whether normies will. GTA VI feels even more inviting to those who just want to spend time in its sandbox to do some fishing, dancing, or flying. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AMD Japan's X account has been met with sharp reproach after claiming the company loves gamers and values its interactions with gamers above all else, with commenters and even a community note expressing dissent at the sentiment, owing to AMD's comments on its "data center-first" ethos and a commitment to AI that has driven the price of consumer PC gaming up to nearly unaffordable levels.

In a recent development, quoting a Tom's Hardware post on the X social network discussing CEO Dr. Lisa Su meeting gamers and autographing a GPU, the AMD Japan account was quick to seize the moment. "AMD values its interactions with gamers above all else," the post read, but it was met with a stark reminder that gamers don't feel the same way. The post soon received a new community note that pointed out that AMD's own CEO doesn't agree. In fact, Su was quoted as saying that AMD is now "a data center-first company," with the note also pointing to the fact that AMD's data center revenue increased 97% year-over-year, as per its Q3 2026 earnings report. That equates to around $8.5 billion in revenue, while client and gaming revenue fell 8% to $3.7 billion. Gaming alone was down 40%.

It has been revealed that at the time, Su said that AMD expected its server revenue to double year over year in 2027, with its data center AI revenue growing at an even faster rate. "As a result, we expect data center to be more than eighty percent of our total revenue in 2027 and to drive the majority of our revenue and earnings growth," the CEO said during the manufacturer's earnings call.

Sources indicate that ゲーマーとの交流を何よりも大切にするAMD。 コミュニティと直接つながり、その声に耳を傾け続ける姿勢こそAMDの強みです。 AMD loves gamers. 🎮November 17, 2026.

By comparison, the same call heard Su say that, in 2027, AMD was "planning for PC market unit shipments to decline by a double-digit percentage." With this all in mind, it's perhaps no surprise that the AMD Japan X account stirred such a strong response from gamers who feel that AMD has left them behind in search of a more lucrative data center market. AMD is certainly not alone in that regard. Nvidia, once the darling of the PC component enthusiast, is now focused on AI data center components instead. The organization's high-performance AI chips are so capable that they're export-controlled, something that, among other reasons, will put former CEO Jensen Huang in front of a House Foreign Affairs panel in December.

As for AMD, its ill-timed, misjudged X post ended with "AMD loves gamers." Gamers would appear to disagree.

A pocket-size book of human anatomy. Solar-powered chargers and small knives. A compass and a road atlas of the continental U.S. That’s what Gina Arconti keeps in her Béis Weekender bag in case of emergencies. “Something some people don’t know about me is I’m a little bit of a doomsday prepper,” she said in a recent TikTok video, now with over 400,000 views. The video was posted last week, after Microsoft Outlook went down. Then flights across the U.S. were grounded. Then Apple Pay stopped working. On Tuesday, the National Security Agency’s classified internal communications network temporarily went down. You don’t have to be a conspiracy theorist to wonder what’s going on. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee on Wednesday that “these are separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes. They are not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack.” But for longtime doomsday preppers, the writing is on the wall. “Amazon doomsday haul,” Jeff For, another TikTok user based in Los Angeles, said in a video posted earlier this month. His purchases include a hand-crank portable radio that doubles as a flashlight, phone charger, compass, and SOS signal. He also bought a collapsible water jug, candles, and a mini drone. “If I’m stuck or I don’t want to leave where I am I can use this bad boy to fly up in the air and see everything around me,” he explains. Some are rushing to stock up on supplies from Costco or $395 emergency backpacks containing everything from a pop-up tube tent to dried ice cream. Others have been squirreling away supplies for years, preparing for this exact moment. Online preppers are also seeing a surge of views amid the outages. “So you just started your prepping journey and you’re not really sure what the next step will be,” said Krystal, known online as the “Doomsday Queen,” to her 132,000 Instagram followers earlier this month. The video’s caption directs viewers to her free Beginner’s Preparedness Guide. View this post on Instagram Others preach off-grid self-sufficiency, offering tutorials on food storage, emergency water supplies, and what to do when the toilets no longer flush. But some may be overlooking the first rule of doomsday prep: Don’t tell anyone about your doomsday prep. Otherwise, where do you think everyone will head when the world actually ends?

#70042. The Nvidia CEO scandal is impacting Asian American women in tech and academia. Here’s how

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2152 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fastcompany ↗ Open Full Page

The Nvidia CEO scandal is impacting Asian American women in tech and academia. Here’s how

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2152 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The reveal earlier this month that billionaire Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had extramarital affairs sent shock waves through the tech world, particularly with Asian Americans who revered him as a once-in-a-generation talent.
  • Industry observers note that the reveal earlier this month that billionaire Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had extramarital affairs sent shock waves through the tech world, particularly with Asian Americans who revered him as a once-in-a-generation talent.
  • According to recent reports, among the social media posts being spread was a collage of photos showing CEOs with Asian female partners.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The reveal earlier this month that billionaire Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had extramarital affairs sent shock waves through the tech world, particularly with Asian Americans who revered him as a once-in-a-generation talent. But what has hit hard for Asian American women is the discourse around the allegation that Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman at the center of the scandal, was possibly a spy.Almost immediately, videos and memes reviving tired tropes fetishizing Asian women hit social media.“So few Asian women in general make it to the news for positive things. This is just going to continue to perpetuate negative stereotypes or biases for Asian women,” said Misa Chien, founder of a network for Asian American women leaders called The Authentic Asian. Whether or not the allegation is true, “just the news will definitely influence people’s opinions of women who have broken the ceiling or are trying to.”Asian American women working in tech, civil rights advocacy and academia have felt a sense of dread that this ordeal will diminish how their peers are viewed and treated in their workplaces. It’s a reminder that no accomplishments will completely dispel centuries-old stereotypes.Jensen Huang has since resigned. However, the U.S. Justice Department has not found sufficient evidence that Alice Huang, who is not related to Jensen Huang, was a spy.“I don’t know if that’s been determined yet,” President Donald Trump told reporters this week. Asian women struggle to be taken seriously as leaders Among the social media posts being spread was a collage of photos showing CEOs with Asian female partners. Author May-lee Chai, who has written about the treatment of Asian women throughout history, called it “disgusting.”Depicting them like trophy wives “implicates these spouses like they’re somehow similar to this suspected spy,” said Chai, a creative writing professor at San Francisco State University.The speed at which people glommed onto the Asian female spy narrative was shocking to April Moh, chief marketing officer for a financial technology company and board member of Stand with Asian Americans, a legal civil rights organization specializing in combating workplace anti-Asian discrimination. The chatter has also led to women sharing stories of uncomfortable interactions.“I have women in technology who tell me that they get really weird looks and they get questioned about laptop security by their colleagues when they’re visiting China,” Moh said. “I have another person telling me that she has been jokingly asked, ‘So, are you a spy?’ by people who think that’s a joke now. It’s not funny to her or me.”Many clients of Stand with Asian Americans are Asian women who have proved their competence yet are still accused of being fraudulent or deceitful, said Rachel Lee, the organization’s president and general counsel.“It is deeply disturbing to see this not just unique to the Nvidia Jensen Huang case, but as a part of a long-standing dangerous narrative that Asians are perpetual foreigners, untrustworthy, disloyal,” Lee said.On top of their integrity being questioned, Asian workers also deal with misconceptions that they cannot lead. The annual Social Tracking of Asian Americans in the United States Index from The Asian American Foundation found at least half of U.S. adults characterized Asian Americans in the workplace as “respectful” or “reliable.” Only 1 in 10 viewed them as “assertive.”“The No. 1 theme in onboarding interviews all last week were ‘I’m mistaken for the secretary, I don’t look like the typical face of leadership,” said Chien, talking about newly introduced members of her Asian leaders network. Stereotypes around Asian women go back centuries Years before Chinese laborers were fully banned from entering the U.S. under the 1882 Chinese Exclusion Act, the federal government targeted immigrant Asian women. In 1875, Congress passed the Page Act to control immigration from “any Oriental country.” It included a specific prohibition of women coming for prostitution.“Chinese women were deemed — and East Asian women in general — as being untrustworthy,” Chai said. “It was presumed that they would be coming for illicit means as prostitutes to the United States and that would cause harm to white men.”By the early 20th century, the Asian woman as a seductress, spy or “dragon lady” started becoming an archetype on Hollywood screens, she added.The headlines had Chien reflecting on when she played a spy in a building security ad in Hong Kong 20 years ago. She was instructed to wear three bras to resemble Angelina Jolie’s figure. She wrote an Instagram post to point out “how the media enjoys putting Asian women in that kind of role” and urged women to not let people’s assumptions keep them from success.“So many followers messaged me saying ‘thank you so much for speaking up,'” Chien said. Real harm can come from stereotypes Suspicion toward Chinese people in the U.S. has dramatically heightened geopolitical tensions. Over two dozen states in the last few years have proposed or enacted “alien land laws” to prevent Chinese nationals from buying property. The number of international students enrolling in American universities has fallen. And the first Trump administration created a plan known as the ” China Initiative ” to crack down on espionage by profiling Chinese professors.Critics say that initiative contributed to the 2024 suicide of Jane Ying Wu. A neuroscientist at Northwestern University who had lived in the U.S. for 40 years, the 60-year-old came under federal investigation in 2019. She was never charged with anything.“This type of pernicious stereotype can actually destroy lives,” Chai said. “It’s not in any way an accurate portrait of an entire race and ethnicity.”Jokes rooted in stereotypes under the guise of being complimentary also do not help Asian female workers, Lee added.“Whether it’s a compliment or not, a trope is a trope,” she said. “I don’t care if it comes out of the mouth of the U.S. president.”Ideally, Lee said more companies should allow for education and training around the harm and history of stereotypes. She encourages any woman who has had uncomfortable interactions to reach out to advocacy groups such as Stand with Asian Americans if she has nobody to turn to at work. At Stand with Asian Americans, people do not need to have a legal case of discrimination or harassment to receive assistance including education on their rights and mental health support.Individuals also have the right to draw boundaries and make clear what’s not OK to say, Lee added. It’s in employers’ best interest to make sure no federal laws against discrimination and harassment are being violated.“It’s a win-win to have that conversation,” Lee said. —Terry Tang, Associated Press.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A strange deal over on Samsung.com is offering the Galaxy Z Fold 8 for $1,499, a new low price for the hit foldable, but it’s not showing up for all people.
  • According to recent reports, samsung’s fresh Galaxy Z Fold 8 is usually sold for $1,899 which, in itself, isn’t a bad price for the device.
  • The discount is available on Samsung.com and cuts $400 off of the price of a upcoming Galaxy Z Fold 8 in any configuration.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A strange deal over on Samsung.com is offering the Galaxy Z Fold 8 for $1,499, a new low price for the hit foldable, but it’s not showing up for all people.

According to recent reports, samsung’s fresh Galaxy Z Fold 8 is usually sold for $1,899 which, in itself, isn’t a bad price for the device. But it’s been available with some kind of discount at basically all times since it launched. And, this week, we’re seeing a new low price that brings the foldable down to $1,499.

The discount is available on Samsung.com and cuts $400 off of the price of a upcoming Galaxy Z Fold 8 in any configuration. That brings the 256GB model down to $1,499.99, as pictured below.

There are two “catches” with this one.

Firstly, this is a discount if you buy the Fold 8 without a trade-in. Moving to a trade charges the fully $1,899 and applies your credit to that.

The other is that, strangely, this $400 discount isn’t showing for everyone. As noted when we covered the previous all-time-low earlier this week, $1,549, Samsung.com only highlights a $350 discount to some customers, and there’s no rhyme or reason to it. As for why this is the case, we’re not sure, but it’s unfortunately not uncommon for Samsung.com sales to act a bit inconsistently like this.

According to recent reports, whatever the case, if you’re hunting for a Galaxy Z Fold 8, now is very much the time. Whether you’re paying $1,549 or $1,499, it’s still a killer discount. Notably, the Amazon deal still lets you stack a trade-in on top for up to $980 off.

DDR6 RAM shrinks by 44% while delivering 4 times more bandwidth than DDR5 — JEDEC previews 12.8 GT/s modules with up to 1 terabyte of capacity per slot

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (703 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that today's best RAM will look huge compared to upcoming DDR6 memory.
  • In a recent development, JEDEC's DDR6 preview highlights improvements in various areas, including performance, capacity, reliability, and power efficiency.
  • Recent findings suggest that one of the most notable differences is that DDR6 memory modules will measure just 74mm in length, 44% shorter than DDR5’s 133mm memory modules.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that today's best RAM will look huge compared to upcoming DDR6 memory. JEDEC has just released a preview of the DDR6 specification, confirming that next-generation memory modules will be 44% shorter than DDR5. That is only the physical aspect, though. From a performance perspective, DDR6 will debut at 12.8 GT/s, more than double DDR5's baseline transfer rate, while also quadrupling the memory bandwidth per memory module thanks to a new design.

In a recent development, JEDEC's DDR6 preview highlights improvements in various areas, including performance, capacity, reliability, and power efficiency. These advancements align with the upgrades DDR5 brought to the table when it debuted.

Recent findings suggest that one of the most notable differences is that DDR6 memory modules will measure just 74mm in length, 44% shorter than DDR5’s 133mm memory modules. This makes DDR6 only 6% longer than DDR5 SO-DIMM modules, which you commonly find in laptops and mini-PCs.

JEDEC has maintained the pin count for many years, sticking to 288 pins for DDR4 and DDR5. However, DDR6 may finally break that mould. Given the substantial reduction in length with DDR6 and the data bus width upgrade, it is reasonable to assume that DDR6 will have a completely different pinout and density. Sadly, JEDEC has not revealed the pin count for DDR6.

Recent findings suggest that early rumors suggested that DDR6 may be limited to CAMM form factors to feed the AI boom. However, JEDEC's announcement at least does not rule out other form factors. It appears JEDEC is still determining which form factors DDR6 will use. Potential options include RDIMM, UDIMM, and CAMM formats, just like DDR5.

Baseline JEDEC Transfer Rates (MT/s).

Baseline JEDEC Bandwidth Per Module (GB/s).

Peak JEDEC Transfer Rates (MT/s).

Peak Baseline Bandwidth Per Module (GB/s).

Notably, JEDEC has increased the data bus width in DDR6 to 96 bits, a 50% boost over DDR5's 64 bits. The channel architecture for DDR6 will also change substantially. While DDR4 and DDR5 leveraged a single 64-bit channel and two 32-bit sub-channels, DDR6 takes a different approach. JEDEC will implement a design with four 24-bit sub-channels.

Using the baseline for comparison, DDR6 offers up to 153.6 GB/s of total module bandwidth, compared to DDR5's 38.4 GB/s. That is a 4X uplift in bandwidth. If we compare DDR5-9200 RDIMMs, which max out at 73.6 GB/s per module, with DDR6-12800 RDIMMs, the uplift is a little more than double.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

Recent findings suggest that at least on the server side, DDR6 RDIMMs will start at DDR6-12800, whereas DDR5 RDIMMs topped out at DDR5-9200. JEDEC anticipates DDR6 reaching DDR6-14400 and beyond. This is for the server and enterprise market, though. It remains to be seen which DDR6 speed will launch in the consumer market. DDR5 commenced at DDR5-4800.

DDR6 may be shorter than DDR5, but it makes up for it by having 2X the bank count. This will help push higher data rates and capacities. DDR6 will support 128Gb (16GB) dies, which represents a massive leap. We are looking at 4X the density of early DDR5 memory modules. Instead of placing chips side by side on the PCB, DDR6 enables die stacking, allowing manufacturers to place multiple dies on top of each other via Through-Silicon Vias (TSVs).

In a recent development, consumer DDR5 memory modules currently sit at 64GB per module, while server RDIMMs have reached 512GB. DDR6 could raise module capacity to 128GB or 256GB and potentially scale RDIMMs to 1TB or more per slot.

Industry observers note that DDR6 has no official launch date. Many believe 2029 is a realistic target for commercialization. However, in the current state of things, it would be a miracle if DDR6 had no setbacks.

Sources indicate that it’s not just tech and AI stocks getting hammered lately. Gold investors are also seeing significant losses. As of this writing, the precious metal is down nearly 3% for the day, trading just above $3,576 per ounce. That’s a level the yellow bullion has not seen since September 2025. That price is all the more striking when contrasted with gold’s surging value earlier this year. In January, gold peaked at around $5,600. But since then, the precious metal has been under constant pressure, and in late September, its price began plummeting from around $4,400 an ounce to roughly $800 less today. But just what is driving gold’s fall as of late? There seem to be three major factors impacting the bullion’s recent plunge. Expected Fed interest rate hikes The first factor likely influencing gold’s fall recently is the likelihood of a federal interest rate hike in December. As Fast Company previously reported, the Fed is likely to raise rates by 25 basis points, to a range of 4.00%–4.25%. When interest rates rise, money becomes more expensive to borrow. This means the lenders of that money stand to make more. Anyone can become a “lender” by buying Treasury bills whose interest rates are heavily tied to the Fed’s set rates. Rising interest rates typically lead investors to sell off non-interest-yielding assets and use the proceeds to buy assets—like Treasury bills—that return a guaranteed rate. This asset reallocation is likely one of the major factors affecting gold prices (and not just gold—but also cryptocurrency prices lately). The tech and AI sell-off The second likely major factor impacting gold prices lately actually has nothing to do with gold itself. Rather, the rut in tech and AI stocks can be to blame. Since October, tech and AI stocks have been under sustained pressure as investors have grown increasingly concerned about what many see as out-of-control, unsustainable capital expenditure by AI hyperscalers. Critics argue that this massive capex spending—to the tune of hundreds of billions—can’t last unless the hyperscalers can start generating sizable returns, something they have so far been unable to do. Investors worry that if revenue (and profits) can’t materialize, the hyperscalers will cut back capex, sending the business of AI component makers like Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Micron, and more into a downward spiral. As these concerns take hold, investors are moving out of high-volatility tech and AI stocks, taking profits and sending shares lower. But not everyone is taking profits. Some investors are cutting their losses, and when they do, they also tend to sell other liquid assets, like gold, to cover them. A stronger U.S. dollar Finally, another problem for gold is the increasing strength of the U.S. dollar. Since September, the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) has increased by more than 4%. The DXY tracks the U.S. dollar’s value relative to six foreign currencies: the Euro, Yen, Pound, Swedish Krona, Swiss Franc, and Canadian Dollar. A strengthening dollar can be a problem for gold because the bullion is priced in U.S. dollars. When U.S. dollars become more valuable relative to foreign currencies, international demand for gold usually slips because it costs foreign investors more to buy the precious metal.

Setting up WireGuard on a small virtual server is a satisfying infrastructure task. Install the package, generate a key pair, open a UDP port, configure a peer, and connect a laptop. Within an afternoon, your staging environment can sit behind a private tunnel, and your internal dashboard can be restricted to traffic from a known address.

The initial setup is rarely the difficult part.

It has been revealed that the real engineering work starts when the team changes. A developer joins, another leaves, someone replaces a laptop, a server needs patching, or a connection suddenly stops working. Each event creates a small maintenance task. Over time, those tasks become an operational responsibility that somebody must own.

This article examines what it takes to operate a self-hosted WireGuard VPN for a development team. We'll look at peer configuration, access management, troubleshooting, monitoring tools, and the engineering time involved. We'll also compare self-hosting with managed business VPN services so teams can make a decision based on their infrastructure needs.

It has been revealed that wireGuard is a modern VPN protocol designed to establish encrypted connections between network peers. Its relatively small codebase, modern cryptography, and straightforward configuration make it attractive for developers who want control over their network infrastructure.

A basic WireGuard deployment typically involves:.

A server with a reachable public IP address.

A private and public key pair for the server.

A key pair for every client device.

A UDP port through which peers communicate.

Peer configuration that defines which addresses are allowed through the tunnel.

A simplified server configuration might look like this:.

The corresponding client configuration contains the client's private key and the server's public key:.

Recent findings suggest that these examples illustrate the basic relationship between a server and a client. A production configuration will also need appropriate firewall rules, routing, DNS settings, and a blueprint for distributing configuration securely.

The important distinction is that WireGuard establishes encrypted peer connections. It does not automatically provide a complete employee identity system, onboarding workflow, approval process, or audit dashboard.

Those responsibilities belong to the team operating the infrastructure.

Developers interested in using WireGuard on personal development devices can also explore SitePoint's guide to building a hardened mobile development environment with Termux, Docker, and WireGuard.

According to recent reports, A peer is not just an entry in a configuration file. It represents a device that has permission to communicate through your network.

That makes peer management an access-control responsibility.

Industry observers note that for a small development team, it is tempting to keep a single configuration file and upgrade it manually whenever someone joins or leaves. This can work initially, but it becomes harder to manage as the number of devices increases.

A useful first step is to maintain a peer inventory:.

The inventory should not contain private keys. Private keys must remain on their respective devices and should never be placed in a shared spreadsheet or source repository.

The inventory instead helps administrators answer practical questions:.

Which person owns this public key?

Which device is associated with this tunnel address?

Is the device still authorized?

When was its access last reviewed?

Has the peer been removed after the device was lost or replaced?

This information becomes especially important when a team uses the VPN to reach staging servers, internal dashboards, databases, or other development resources.

Manual onboarding is manageable when a team has only two or three developers. It becomes unreliable when several people join, leave, or change devices over the year.

A repeatable onboarding process should cover more than generating a key pair.

A practical workflow looks like this:.

Confirm that the team member is authorized to access the environment.

Generate a key pair on the user's device.

Assign a unique tunnel address.

Add the public key to the server's peer configuration.

Apply the appropriate routing and firewall permissions.

Deliver the client configuration through a secure channel.

Test access to the specific development resources the person needs.

Record the peer owner, device, and approval details.

Offboarding needs an equally clear process:.

Identify every peer associated with the departing team member.

Remove the relevant public keys from the server.

Confirm that the configuration change has been applied.

Review any other credentials or allowlists that granted access.

Record when access was revoked.

An administrator can inspect the currently configured peers with:.

Recent findings suggest that the output helps identify peer public keys, transfer counters, and latest handshake information. It is useful for troubleshooting, but it should not be treated as a complete access audit or proof that a particular person is still authorized.

The broader lesson is to make access changes part of a documented workflow. A peer should not remain active simply because nobody remembers who created it.

One common network-design mistake is assuming that connecting to a VPN should give a developer access to every internal service.

That is not necessarily the right model.

A developer working on a frontend application may need access to a staging web server but not to the production database. A contractor may need access to one test environment without being able to reach internal administration tools.

WireGuard's peer configuration and the surrounding network controls should be designed around those requirements.

For example, teams can combine:.

Separate tunnel address ranges for different groups.

Firewall rules that restrict traffic to approved services.

Cloud security groups that limit access to specific ports.

Application-level authentication for internal dashboards.

Separate production and staging network boundaries.

Industry observers note that the exact implementation depends on the infrastructure. The key point is that VPN membership and application authorization are different controls.

A successful VPN handshake should not be treated as permission to access every resource behind the tunnel.

It has been revealed that A VPN can appear simple when it works. Diagnosing it becomes more complicated when a developer is connecting from a home router, a hotel network, or a mobile hotspot.

DNS resolving to an unexpected address.

Incorrect routing or AllowedIPs settings.

Firewall rules blocking UDP traffic.

MTU problems that affect larger packets.

A peer using an outdated configuration.

A server process or host becoming unavailable.

WireGuard provides useful inspection commands:.

These commands help inspect peer information, check the service state, and review recent service logs. The exact systemd service name can differ depending on how the interface was configured.

In a recent development, administrators should also monitor the underlying server. At minimum, that means checking:.

Whether the WireGuard interface is active.

Whether the UDP port is reachable.

Whether disk or memory usage is approaching a limit.

Whether operating-system and package updates are pending.

A small virtual server may be inexpensive, but it is still infrastructure that needs an owner.

Recent findings suggest that teams working with alternative tunnel-based development workflows may find SitePoint's tutorial on setting up Cloudflare Tunnels with Docker Compose for persistent webhook debugging useful. It covers a different tunneling use case, but the operational questions around connectivity, service health, and troubleshooting are closely related.

A self-hosted VPN does not need to become a collection of manual tasks. A few established tools can make configuration, monitoring, and debugging more repeatable.

Industry observers note that the core tool is, of course, WireGuard. Its command-line utilities allow administrators to inspect peers, manage interfaces, and review connection information. The official documentation is the best starting point for understanding configuration options and platform support.

Recent findings suggest that ansible can automate repeatable server administration tasks. A team could use playbooks to deploy configuration files, apply system updates, or standardize firewall settings across several VPN hosts.

In a recent development, sensitive values should be handled with an appropriate secrets-management approach. Private keys should not be committed to a Git repository or stored in plaintext playbooks.

Prometheus is useful for collecting and querying metrics, while Node Exporter exposes Linux host metrics such as CPU, memory, disk, and network statistics.

These tools do not automatically provide a complete WireGuard security audit. They can, however, help identify resource problems and server-health concerns before those problems become user-reported outages.

It has been revealed that uptime Kuma provides a self-hosted monitoring dashboard with notifications. It can help teams monitor the availability of a VPN host or related services.

A basic availability check does not prove that every VPN peer can connect successfully. For more meaningful monitoring, combine host checks with an end-to-end test from a separate network.

Wireshark and tcpdump help developers inspect network traffic when diagnosing connectivity problems.

For example, tcpdump can capture UDP traffic on the WireGuard port:.

This can help determine whether packets are reaching the server. It does not decrypt WireGuard traffic or replace checks of routing, firewall rules, and peer configuration.

Recent findings suggest that the right toolset depends on the size of the deployment. A team with one VPN server may only need WireGuard's own commands and basic host monitoring. A larger environment may benefit from automation, centralized metrics, and a documented incident process.

According to recent reports, A self-hosted VPN can cost very little in direct infrastructure charges. However, the server invoice does not include the engineering time required to operate it.

Consider a hypothetical team with these assumptions:.

Two people join and two leave during the year.

The team reviews or rotates device keys quarterly.

Patching and monitoring require about two hours per month.

Six troubleshooting incidents occur annually.

The estimated loaded engineering cost is $60 per hour.

The virtual server costs approximately $6 per month.

The following estimate illustrates how quickly maintenance time can exceed the infrastructure bill.

According to recent reports, at $60 per hour, 46 hours represent approximately $2,760 in engineering time. The server adds around $72 per year, bringing the estimated total to $2,832.

These figures are illustrative, not a universal cost benchmark. A team with infrastructure automation and established monitoring may spend considerably less time. A team with frequent staff changes or strict audit requirements may spend more.

The useful exercise is to measure the work your own team performs. Track onboarding, access reviews, patching, incidents, and recovery time for a few months. That gives you a more realistic comparison than looking at hosting prices alone.

Self-hosting is not automatically the best option just because a team has developers who can configure servers.

A managed business VPN may be worth considering when the team needs centralized member management, simpler device administration, or a stable network exit address without maintaining the underlying VPN infrastructure.

Depending on the provider and blueprint, managed services may offer:.

A central dashboard for adding and removing consumers.

Dedicated or shared IP options.

Client applications for common operating systems.

Multi-factor authentication or identity integrations.

Centralized administration and support.

For example, PureVPN for Teams is one service in this category. Teams evaluating it—or any other provider—should check the current feature set, pricing, logging practices, access controls, and service terms before making a decision.

Recent findings suggest that A managed service does not remove every security responsibility. The team still needs to decide who receives access, review permissions, protect user accounts, and understand how traffic and metadata are handled.

In a recent development, it also introduces vendor dependency and a recurring subscription cost. Those trade-offs should be considered alongside the engineering time saved.

There are situations where running WireGuard yourself is the more practical option.

Industry observers note that you already operate infrastructure. If your team routinely patches servers, manages secrets, monitors services, and responds to incidents, maintaining a VPN may add relatively little work.

You need custom routing. A deployment that connects several private cloud networks, on-premises environments, or specialized subnets may require network controls that are easier to implement directly.

You have strict data-control requirements. Some organizations have policies that limit which third parties can handle network traffic or related metadata. Those requirements may favor infrastructure under the organization's own control.

You have a dedicated platform or security team. If someone is explicitly responsible for access management, monitoring, and incident response, self-hosting can fit naturally into existing operations.

In a recent development, you can automate the lifecycle. Infrastructure-as-code, configuration management, documented peer inventories, and tested recovery procedures can reduce repetitive work and make a self-hosted deployment easier to maintain.

The notable distinction is between a deliberately operated service and a one-off server that nobody owns.

Before choosing an approach, ask the following questions:.

Who is responsible for the VPN six or twelve months after deployment?

How many people and devices are likely to join or leave?

How are public keys and peer configurations tracked?

How quickly can access be revoked when a device is lost?

Which internal services should each developer be able to reach?

Do you need a fixed egress IP for external allowlists?

What monitoring and recovery process exists if the server fails?

Do your customers or internal policies require access logs or formal reviews?

Does your team have the time and expertise to maintain the infrastructure?

Would a managed service cost less than the engineering time and operational risk it replaces?

If your team already has mature infrastructure practices and needs custom network control, self-hosting may be a sensible choice.

If the team is small, access changes frequently, and nobody has time to own another server, a managed service may be more practical.

According to recent reports, wireGuard is an excellent protocol, and deploying it can be a straightforward engineering task. But operating a VPN for a development team involves more than establishing an encrypted connection.

Peer management, onboarding, offboarding, network permissions, monitoring, patching, and troubleshooting all require ongoing attention.

The right choice depends on the team's infrastructure experience, security requirements, size, and available engineering time. Self-hosting offers control and flexibility; a managed service can reduce operational work. Neither option removes the need for sound access-control practices.

Before deciding, calculate the maintenance effort, identify who will own the service, and make sure the design can be maintained as the team changes.

The cost example uses illustrative assumptions rather than current vendor pricing. Managed VPN features and prices can change, so verify provider details before purchasing.

Critical Java vulnerability puts millions of sites, services, and devices at risk of remote code execution

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (582 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the flaw was dubbed Java4Shell by Calif Research, the lab that found the vulnerability.
  • You can see an exploit of the bug in action below across multiple software services.
  • The actual bug is a flaw in an optimization for Base64 decoding, functionality that's ubiquitous in any programming language.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the flaw was dubbed Java4Shell by Calif Research, the lab that found the vulnerability. The researchers say it rates 9.2 on the newer CVSS 4.0 scale, though individual reports from companies like Oracle itself and Red Hat give it their own ratings, but they're all in the 8 to 9.8 range depending on the vendor. The root cause is a bug in OpenJDK, the library that nearly every distribution of Java, whether Oracle's or anyone else's, derives their implementations from.

You can see an exploit of the bug in action below across multiple software services.

The actual bug is a flaw in an optimization for Base64 decoding, functionality that's ubiquitous in any programming language. Base64 is a format to allow for easy transformation of binary data into plain text. In the modern day, it's used to embed files in the middle of text, like inserting image data in the middle of HTML or CSS, attaching files to emails (internally they're all text-based), or simply representing data as text for visual inspection, like file checksums or cryptographic key fingerprints.

Sources indicate that oracle has already fixed the bug and issued updated versions of its wares. However, much like digital certificates, operating systems and even individual programs include their own copy of a Java executable, meaning that the potential blast radius is far wider than you'd expect at first glance. Calif listed many such common applications: at the time of the post, Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, and PingFederate all had full unauthenticated RCE, while Apache Kafka Broker, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker have RCEs after authentication.

Industry observers note that because Java is so darn widespread, most every company has to glitch security advisories and updates for their wares, including IBM, Red Hat, Siemens, and Broadcom. Because so many containers also use Java-based applications in some form, those too are vulnerable, and the count of individual vulnerable container images across registries everywhere is likely a high figure. This is likely not a bug that will be easily eradicated.

It has been revealed that there is a condition to trigger the exploit, but it's not too difficult to fulfill. The Java instance in question must be running on an x86-64 CPU with AVX-512 support and the VBMI extension. In practice, that means chips from the Intel Ice Lake and AMD Zen 4 families, from 2021 and 2022 respectively, for their server variants. Older CPUs are not affected, as the code optimization that contains the bug is specific to VBMI.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

In a recent development, the specific bug is in a hand-written assembly optimization that fails a simple bounds check. If an attacker inputs 64 As and an "=" sign as padding, they can overwrite neighboring memory, and then weaponize that corruption, similar to how Heartbleed worked. As usual these days, Calif states that the vulnerability was found by an AI bot, with $200 worth of tokens. Though unlike many other examples, this one was actually fairly deep, and it wasn't low-hanging fruit that illustrated poor code or network security hygiene.

He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music demonstrates and festivals.
